title: add RAG agent tool-calling examples and docs quickstarts
author: Aisha Patel
description: Add RAG agent tool-calling examples and quickstart docs. This PR provides: 1) three new RAG agent templates (faq-bot, code-assistant, finance-retriever) demonstrating tool-calling integrations with external HTTP data sources and a local query tool; 2) language-specific quickstarts for Python and TypeScript showing end-to-end setup, token handling, streaming, and structured JSON output; 3) docs site navigation and landing page updates linking the new quickstarts and templates; and 4) small SDK example tweaks to make the tool-calling API ergonomics clearer. Motivation: make it faster for engineers to prototype retrieval-augmented agents that call external tools while preserving Redwood platform best practices (KV caching, prefix caching, and safe tool sandboxing). Checklist: - [x] Add RAG agent templates and example configs - [x] Add Python quickstart with runnable example - [x] Add TypeScript quickstart with runnable example - [x] Update docs site nav and landing page - [x] Add tests for example-templates smoke runs - [x] Update SDK examples for tool-calling docs - [x] Add release notes entry

release_notes: Added RAG agent templates (faq-bot, code-assistant, finance-retriever) and tool-calling quickstarts for Python and TypeScript. Docs site updated with a quickstarts landing page. Small SDK example improvements for tool-calling ergonomics.
notes_for_backport: No runtime changes; docs/examples only. No backport required for release branches.
additional_context: These examples are intended as reference implementations. The http tool in templates uses a simple retry/backoff policy; production integrations should replace with authenticated connectors and follow KMS/HSM guidance for secrets. Smoke tests are lightweight and run in CI using mocked endpoints.
